text: Forensic note on the death of this world, restored to year 8500 from archive. At year 8525 the simulation went non-finite and kept running for eight hundred more years -- writing NaN over every checkpoint, serving NaN in summary.json, and reporting TOTAL FAUNAL EXTINCTION to nobody at all. The only clean state that survived was the year 8500 century archive, which is where the world now stands. Nothing between 8500 and 9329 can be recovered; those eight hundred years are gone. What happened, in order. gut_ferment was added at year 8133 with +0.7 to plant_digest and another +0.35 in plains. By year 8500 it had swept the entire population -- mean 0.918, every animal above half -- and plant digestion averaged 1.649 against a baseline of 1.0, so a mouthful of grass carried about sixty-five per cent more energy than it used to. Between years 8505 and 8524 the world then went up like a balloon: flora from 2,964 to 69,945 and fauna from 837 to 18,074 against a cap of 20,000, in nineteen years. The mechanism is not mysterious -- animals that need less biomass for the same energy graze less, so the plants recover, which feeds more animals. At 8525 the arithmetic broke and by 8526 everything was dead. The corruption itself was an engine fault and it is fixed: the lithosphere reservoir was guarded with `<= 0`, which NaN passes because NaN compares false to everything, and it then multiplied that NaN into soil fertility across every cell a disaster touched. It is guarded properly now, checkpointing refuses to write a world containing non-finite values so a good save can never again be overwritten by a broken one, and the warning appears in summary.json before any other check runs. What I have deliberately not done is retire gut_ferment. The population is wholly adapted to it, and removing it would cut the food supply of every animal alive by something like forty per cent -- which would probably finish what the NaN started. The boom on its own is survivable; this world carried twenty thousand animals at year 1000 and came down from it without dying. It was the corruption that killed, not the crowd. But the gene is still armed, it will do the same thing again, and you should decide with open eyes whether a trait that doubles the energy in the world's food supply is one this world should keep. A weaker replacement is available to you: retire it and add one at a third of the magnitude.
